option.counterfactual: Every positive sequence in a finite AW*-factor whose partial sums are bounded by 1 has quasitrace values tending to zero. In particular, positive quasitrace values bounded away from zero cannot occur under that bound.
option.approach: Investigate quasitracial estimates for bounded signed sums of positive elements. A suitable finite-cotype inequality would force individual quasitrace values to vanish without assuming additivity.

judge.reason: It claims an exact value for the set, and that value is identical to e1.

options.counterfactual: A finite AW*-factor can contain positive elements whose partial sums are bounded by 1 while their faithful normalized 2-quasitrace values stay bounded away from zero. Thus the exhaustion statement used to exclude constant increments is false.
options.approach: Scale each positive element individually to give it the same positive quasitrace value, checking that the scaling coefficients are at most 1. Then investigate separately whether the resulting increasing partial sums have a least upper bound.

options.counterfactual: A finite AW*-factor can contain positive elements whose partial sums are bounded by 1 while their faithful normalized 2-quasitrace values stay bounded away from zero. Thus the exhaustion statement used to exclude constant increments is false.
options.approach: Investigate order continuity of the canonical quasitrace at zero. If an increasing sequence has supremum a, its residuals a-a_n decrease to zero, so an appropriate order-continuity theorem could exclude uniformly positive quasitrace increments despite failure of general exhaustion.

options.counterfactual: A finite AW*-factor can contain positive elements whose partial sums are bounded by 1 while their faithful normalized 2-quasitrace values stay bounded away from zero. Thus the exhaustion statement used to exclude constant increments is false.
options.approach: Audit the proposed finite-cotype route by identifying precisely which inequality would convert bounded signed sums into vanishing quasitrace values. Determine whether that inequality is actually known or whether its purported proof silently assumes additivity.

options.counterfactual: Every bounded increasing self-adjoint sequence in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound. Consequently, the no-least-upper-bound requirement is impossible independently of quasitrace exhaustion.
options.approach: Verify the exact monotone sequential completeness theorem and its hypotheses, distinguishing ordinary order completeness from completeness of the projection lattice and spectral order. If applicable, use it directly to exclude every proposed witness.

options.approach: Attempt to reconstruct sequential completeness through quasitrace-metric limits. Check separately whether bounded sets are complete, whether the positive cone is closed, and whether bounded increasing sequences are necessarily Cauchy.

options.approach: Investigate whether finiteness and AW* projection joins allow a direct construction of a supremum using compatible compressions or graph projections. Track the step that passes from projection completeness to the ordinary self-adjoint order.

options.counterfactual: There exists a witness satisfying all the problem's requirements with eta equal to 1/2, including the absence of a least upper bound.
options.approach: Examine the proposed endpoint construction and verify every hypothesis independently: the AW* annihilator property, factoriality, finiteness, the faithful normalized matrix-extendible quasitrace, and the no-supremum condition.

options.approach: Use positive scaling of the endpoint witness to construct witnesses for smaller parameters. Combine this with the two-increment monotonicity bound to obtain an exact determination of the set.
